reason: Ahmedabad: the premises (Mundra), the Lessor (Gandhidham) and the Lessee (Ghaziabad) are all elsewhere, so nothing connects it, and parties cannot confer jurisdiction (A.B.C. Laminart). Rule: void when nothing in the deed (the premises, a party's office, the place of signing or of payment) connects the named city; refer when one of these does, as in PO-16 and PO-61.
Bangalore: the premises, both offices and the signing are in Hyderabad, so nothing connects it (A.B.C. Laminart). Article XXIII does not save it. Rule as for TE-003.
Chennai: the land, both offices and the signing are in Hyderabad, so nothing connects it (A.B.C. Laminart). Rule as for TE-003.
Chennai (cl. I(h)): the premises and the Lessor are in Coimbatore, the Lessee in Bangalore, and the deed was signed at Coimbatore, so nothing connects it (A.B.C. Laminart). Rule as for TE-003.
Pune: the premises are in Gurgaon, the Lessor in New Delhi and the Lessee in Mumbai, so nothing connects it (A.B.C. Laminart). Rule as for TE-003.

'May' does not contradict cl. 5A's 'shall', so 5A is the arbitration agreement and the bar is its ordinary effect. Who appoints is for s.11 (Perkins Eastman). The bar cannot remove the courts' role under ss. 9, 11, 34 and 36 of the 1996 Act.
Cls. 5A and 12A bind the parties to arbitrate any dispute, so the court exclusion is the ordinary effect of arbitration (Enercon), subject to the courts' role under the 1996 Act.

'They may agree to go to arbitration': they already have, in cls. 5A and 12A, so 'neither of them may go to court' is the ordinary effect of arbitration, subject to the courts' role under the 1996 Act.

Arbitration only if both agree 'at the time the dispute arises' contradicts cl. 23A's present promise to arbitrate. Which prevails (the earlier clause, Ramkishore Lal, against the courts' lean towards arbitration) is for a court.
The Lessor's opinion is not made final and no forum is excluded. A s.28 look-alike, not outside scope: it concerns who decides what is due, not what can be recovered.

The Lessee may take a dispute about its share to arbitration under cl. 16. Rule: cite Exception 1 when a clause is valid because the dispute can go to arbitration; cite s.28 when it is valid because the courts stay open.
